title: Prevent Engram MCP self-deadlock on cold runtime dispatch
outcome: After process restart, dispatch_turn owns the global StateInner mutex while starting an idle runtime. The new Engram MCP config lookup reacquires the same non-reentrant mutex through engram_mcp_stdio_config_for_session, deadlocking the request and every state-dependent route. Pass a lock-safe configuration snapshot into runtime startup and add regression coverage.
acceptance: Cold Claude runtime dispatch can build its MCP configuration without reacquiring StateInner; existing Claude, Codex, and ACP Engram MCP configuration behavior remains covered; focused tests and required quality gates pass.

completion.summary:
Closed with evidence; the fix was already on master.

Commit 13573d9 (2026-08-28) makes cold Claude dispatch (turn_dispatch.rs) and session-config startup (session_config.rs) build the Claude MCP config from an Engram descriptor taken by engram_mcp_stdio_config_for_session_locked. The caller already holds StateInner, so nothing re-locks the mutex.

Evidence at master 169fc8b, in the named root .tmp/wt-p0-close-9474:
- pinned by claude_mcp_snapshot_composition_is_state_lock_safe and cold_claude_turn_start_does_not_reenter_state_mutex_for_engram_config: the focused run passed 2 of 2, verification 3b53e530;
- the credited full gate test-d09db305 passed all five stages;
- independent evaluation delegation-f603d078 (Codex) passed 1 of 1.
The first evaluation, delegation-873fea6b, was insufficient-evidence until the gate was credited on this item.

The landing commit and time are the fix commit's own; the original push time is not recorded.
